newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone coup leaders seek diplomatic deal.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone coup leaders seek diplomatic deal.

text.p: Sierra Leone's military coup leaders, facing the threat of attack by a Nigerian-led regional force, have intensified diplomatic contacts to seek a way out of the crisis, diplomatic sources said on Sunday.
"They sent a delegation which met the Nigerian ambassador. Basically they wanted assurances of safe conduct outside the country and possible asylum," said a source close to the talks.
The representatives of the coup leaders who met ambassador Chidi Abubakar at his residence included the number two in the new Armed Forces Revolutionary Council (AFRC), Captain Paul Thomas.
"The ambassador told them Nigeria would consider their request but could not speak for other countries on the issue of asylum," the source said.

The talks took place on Saturday as military sources reported that a contingent of Guinean troops had entered Sierra Leone to join the Nigerian-led regional force gearing up to reverse the week-old coup by junior officers in Freetown.
Diplomats said representatives of the coup leaders had also held talks with British envoys and U.N. officials.

The situation was complicated by the fact that the coup had been largely hijacked by Sierra Leone rebels who had waged an armed campaign since 1991 and were opposed to any negotiations, the diplomats said.
Revolutionary United Front (RUF) rebels entered the capital Freetown in large numbers after last Sunday's coup toppled the civilian government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

They were welcomed as allies by the coup plotters but appear to have increased their influence at the military headquarters where coup leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah and his colleagues have been holed up since seizing power.
Koromah, who had been detained for plotting against the former civilian government, has not been seen in public since he was freed from Freetown's maximum security prison at the start of the coup.
In the past two days RUF spokesmen have broadcast a stream of statements on state radio, many of them markedly more hardline in tone than those from the AFRC.
One statement said the RUF had brought 5,000 men from its long-running bush war and would fight any intervention force to the end.
It called for the release of RUF leader Foday Sankoh who has been detained in Nigeria.
Sankoh was moved from a luxury hotel in the Nigerian capital Abuja to prison custody last week after urging his men to join the coup soldiers, Nigerian military sources said.
Diplomats and West African military officers said RUF commanders had hardened their stance since the coup leaders opened diplomatic contacts.

This increased the prospect of a military strike by the Nigerian-led West African force ECOMOG, whose strength in Sierra Leone was boosted on Saturday by the arrival of three battalions of Guinean troops.
The United Nations, the Organisation of African Unity and the West African alliance ECOWAS have condemned the coup and called for restoration of power to Kabbah, who fled to Guinea.
Nigeria landed more troops and equipment in Freetown on Saturday. A Nigerian Air Force plane brought armoured personnel carriers and soldiers to Hastings airport on the eastern outskirts.
ECOMOG, whose main mandate is keeping peace in Liberia, now has about 3,000 men in Sierra Leone. They are backed by Nigerian ships lying offshore as well as helicopters based in Liberia.
Foreigners have been fleeing from Sierra Leone by air and sea. Widespread looting and violence erupted after the coup.
A French navy frigate ferried about 200 Europeans to Guinea on Saturday, a day after U.S. marines airlifted some 900 Westerners out of Freetown.
